headline: Congress cancels a 2024 federal rule that changed how bank merger applications are reviewed by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.
what_it_does: This law uses the Congressional Review Act to cancel a rule issued in September 2024 by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), a Treasury office that oversees national banks. That rule changed how the OCC reviews requests from banks that want to merge. Among other things, it ended automatic approvals under a faster review process and stopped the use of shorter application forms. With the rule canceled, it has no legal effect.

who_it_affects.group: National banks and federal savings associations planning mergers
who_it_affects.how: Their merger applications will no longer be reviewed under the procedures set by the canceled 2024 rule.

who_it_affects.group: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
who_it_affects.how: The agency cannot enforce the 2024 rule and, under the Congressional Review Act, cannot issue a substantially similar rule unless Congress later authorizes it.
